findings.title: DMARC policy is "none" — monitoring only, no enforcement
findings.detail: A DMARC policy of "none" means emails that fail authentication are still delivered. This provides reporting data but offers no protection against spoofing.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to p=quarantine (routes to spam) or p=reject (blocks delivery) once legitimate email flows are verified.

findings.title: DMARC record has no aggregate reporting address (rua)
findings.detail: Without a reporting address, you will not receive DMARC aggregate reports showing who is sending email on behalf of your domain.
findings.recommendation: Add rua=mailto:dmarc@yourdomain.com to your DMARC record.

findings.title: No DKIM record found
findings.detail: DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing emails, allowing recipients to verify they were sent by an authorised server and have not been tampered with.
findings.evidence: Checked selectors: default, google, mail, k1, selector1, selector2, dkim, s1, s2. None found at {selector}._domainkey.genpet.org
findings.recommendation: Configure DKIM through your email provider and publish the public key as a TXT record at the appropriate selector.
